title: topic-record.v0
description: One topic from a three-space reconstruction, carried as a GROUNDED record rather than a bare term-list. The distinction is the whole point: the compressed ('seven-word') form of a topic is just its top terms; the faithful form keeps the label, the reasoning connecting the statistical signature to what was actually happening, and the REPRESENTATIVE EVIDENCE (real snippets, not the label). A topic-record maps 1:1 onto the graph brain: label+reasoning+mass IS a claim.v0, and each representative_evidence item IS an evidence.v0 — so a reconstruction is a first-class producer into Crystal Atlas. A record is 'grounded' ONLY when it carries both reasoning and non-empty evidence; a label alone is never trusted.

reasoning.description: Why these terms mean this label — the analytical trail that compaction normally drops. Required for grounded=true.

representative_evidence.description: The actual snippets the corpus surfaced as most characteristic. Each item is an evidence.v0 (doc_id=source_ref, snippet=the witness bytes, score). A doc_id without a snippet is a pointer with no witness — rejected by the validator.

grounded.description: TRUE only when reasoning is present AND representative_evidence is non-empty. Enforced by the validator — this is the term-list-vs-faithful distinction made into teeth.
